automation_evidence.quote: We therefore study corrective feature discovery: automatically finding interpretable features of the residual, the signal of where and how a particular frozen forecaster fails.

metric_evidence.quote: Under the shared harness of §4, both C RAFTER variants outperform each of the three dedicated feature-engineering systems, with per-baseline paired Wilcoxon tests significant at p<0.01.

evidence.quote: The clearest case is EPF. External banks and syntactic search add little beyond the covariate-only corrector, while C RAFTER removes much more of the frozen error

practical_problems.note: Source-blind gate isolates the feature source: covariate-only corrector, syntactic search and external feature banks versus LLM-named semantic features.

evidence.quote: We test this by replaying the features accepted on one split onto a later split, with the LLM and search turned off, so only the feature set's origin changes

practical_problems.note: Replay of accepted features across ordered split pairs against self and covariate-only bounds; performance decays mildly with split distance.

summary: An agent mines a frozen forecaster's residuals for LLM-named and searched corrective features behind a source-blind gate; it beats feature-engineering baselines, and controls isolate feature source and cross-split transfer.
